title: Desktop: keep native file choosers off the event loop
body:
## What and why

Closes #683. Native Open, Save, Save As, embedded-model save, import, deck export and CSV export currently enter a blocking OS file dialog from the app event loop. The desktop host now returns an `rfd::AsyncFileDialog` future. The app polls only a pending chooser and schedules repaint while it is pending, including the first poll when a toolbar action creates the chooser after frame logic. Idle frames do not poll a chooser or gain a periodic repaint.

Only one chooser can be pending. A selection is discarded if the model, current document identity, path or revision changes, or if a background job has started. New/Open/sample/update continuations run only after the selected save actually succeeds; cancellation or a write failure keeps the current document. Existing explicit-path/programmatic commands retain their normal no-dialog result contract. The browser retains its existing picker behavior.

Every chooser starts from a fresh clone of a builder parented to the actual FieldCraft window through `CreationContext` and `AsyncFileDialog::set_parent`. This supplies the parent to the Wayland portal and the Windows/macOS chooser without retaining a borrowed creation context or accumulating filters and names across requests.

`ui.inspect` exposes `file_picker` so control clients can distinguish a pending host chooser from app forms; the control protocol documentation is updated. There are no dependency, solver, ROADMAP or GPU-backend changes.

Validation on Linux CPU at `4dd0eae4e026dd0db97316efe55c342f362ee7b9`:

- `cargo check -p fieldcraft -p fieldcraft-ui-egui`.
- Desktop app and UI tests: 8 desktop tests and 202 UI tests passed, zero failures. Only those test binaries ran; the build retained the existing cached package feature resolution plus the desktop app. UI doctests: 3 passed through direct `rustdoc` using the freshly compiled UI library, its exact 18 direct-dependency/self artifacts, build-script native search paths and Cargo compile environment.
- `cargo clippy -p fieldcraft -p fieldcraft-ui-egui --all-targets -- -D warnings`, formatting and diff checks.
- Manual simplification review. No new dependencies, unsafe code, command schemas, numerical changes or fixtures.

This session has no configured Wayland or X11 desktop session or Wayland compositor, so the requested native Wayland Save/Cancel check remains pending. No GPU or new native desktop validation is claimed.

Historical demonstration from the original `b485880d04f0005232e9e24fc7f5cfbd79f12e3f` capture follows. These attachments show the pre-parent-fix source; they are retained with their original provenance and do not validate the parent-window correction.

A 24-second Windows native evidence clip shows the genuine OS Save As window, then seven selected, actually presented app frames while that same chooser is pending and the camera changes. The chooser is captured separately because it is an OS window; an explicitly marked opaque redaction covers only the private folder/search breadcrumb. Its type/Save/Cancel controls are original pixels. The app frames are not presented as screenshots of the chooser.

On Windows 11 with an NVIDIA GeForce RTX 4090 Vulkan viewport, eight bounded `ui.inspect` calls returned while `file_picker` was true; the slowest roundtrip was 0.0110964 seconds with a two-second timeout. The app rendered all seven camera frames through the native presented-frame capture path. This is responsiveness evidence, not a throughput benchmark. At the unchanged base `7d9c027`, the same real Save As interaction caused two two-second control timeouts and responded again after native Cancel.

The executable was built after the exact requested commit. Its SHA-256 is `d4ed882e0b0510135fa8106015b9dd5d779f67bb0a73d4e26ff08274a5398e27`; the original 315-node/160-hex model remained byte-identical after the demonstration. The owned app and chooser were closed through `app.quit` after capture.

`async-native-file-chooser.mp4`, `native-chooser.png` and `responsive-viewport.png` were transferred as ordinary Git blobs by the coordinator in artifact-queue commit `c453484333dd6fecd51ac64396409d69cc647b51`, under `objects/fix/async-file-dialogs-683/b485880d04f0005232e9e24fc7f5cfbd79f12e3f/`. Index SHA-256 hashes and byte sizes were verified before the normal push. The maintainer's receipts confirm all three artifacts received, with SHA-256 hashes and byte counts matching their manifests; `github_attachment` is now `attached` with the verified native URLs below. Private logs, unredacted chooser capture and the original capture/encoding recipe are retained externally. No demonstration binaries, raster images or LFS pointers are in the feature history.

Native GitHub attachments (original capture revision `b485880d04f0005232e9e24fc7f5cfbd79f12e3f`; receipts verify the original SHA-256 and byte sizes):

- [async-native-file-chooser.mp4](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/e9ceecf5-edbf-418a-be06-e48faafb73a4)
- [native-chooser.png](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/c9382c74-e09f-4dbc-b5a9-3ca993d50e2a)
- [responsive-viewport.png](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/ccd8a942-f079-468c-b71c-b055cf0ea471)

Known limits: native Save/Cancel completion with the parented chooser still needs a Wayland desktop check; macOS and Windows completion behavior was not rerun. The original Windows input helper could capture the chooser but could not activate it, so its historical clip demonstrates pending-dialog responsiveness, not native Save/Cancel completion. Deferred-host tests cover successful selection, cancellation, failed writes and guarded continuations separately. No full local CI gate, wasm gate, numerical oracle or performance study was run for this review revision.

reviews.author: jyviko
reviews.body:
Really nice work, thank you! I read rfd 0.17.2 for each platform: the portal call runs on its own thread on Linux, Windows runs its own dialog thread, and macOS uses a sheet polled on the main thread, so the main-thread rule holds. Dropping stale choices when the model or revision changes is a thoughtful touch.

One ask: please pass the parent window with `set_parent` (`apps/fieldcraft/src/main.rs:41`). Otherwise the Wayland portal and the Windows chooser aren't tied to FieldCraft's window and can open behind it. If you can try Save/Cancel once on Wayland, that would close #683 for real.

reviews.author: jyviko
reviews.body:
Reviewed. As far as I can tell from rfd 0.17.2, the threading is sound: the portal runs on a worker thread with a oneshot channel on Linux, a window-modal sheet runs on the main thread with a callback on macOS, and a worker thread handles Windows. I see no deadlock path, rfd stays in the app crate, and the web build is unaffected.

1. You note that macOS and Wayland completion haven't been run, and the macOS path is now a sheet. We'll run it on a Mac before merging. If you can test Wayland, please add the result.
2. Optional: `files.rs:610` polls with `Waker::noop()` and repaints every 50 ms while a chooser is open (`lib.rs:2180`, `:2359`). rfd wakes its waker on completion, so a waker that calls `ctx.request_repaint()` would replace the polling.
3. Pre-existing, not introduced here (fine as a follow-up): over the control channel, `ui.prompt {"answer":"save"}` on an untitled model calls `answer_unsaved` (`control.rs:419`), which opens a native chooser (`files.rs:1115`). That breaks "programmatic calls never open dialogs".
